answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of non-sequential compute-proof-work per identity to act as a resilient gateway for the network. The verifier enforces this by checking if every hash output matches a unique, ephemeral task, treating each identity like a delicate yarrow stalk that must be earned by raw energy. While an honest agent pays this cost once, an attacker trying to flood the network with 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 puzzles, effectively reading a somber sonnet of processing exhaustion. Any found fraud triggers a permanent burn of the sable identity, though we assume no compute.
